source_text: Τὸ δοκεῖν δὲ, ἂν μὲν ὑπάρχῃ, δεξόμεθα, ἵν' εἴπω τι καὶ ἀνθρώπινον· ἂν δὲ ἀντιπίπτῃ, χαίρειν ἐάσομεν, καὶ οὐδὲν τοῦ εἶναι διὰ τὸ δοκεῖν ἀφαι-ρήσομεν. Θʹ. Καὶ γὰρ οὕτως ἔχει· ὁ μέν τινος ἕνεκεν τὸ καλὸν ἐπιτηδεύων, οὐ βέβαιος εἰς ἀρετήν. Ὁμοῦ τε γὰρ παρῆλθεν ἐκεῖνο, καὶ τοῦ καλοῦ στήσεται· ὥσπερ ὁ κέρδους ἕνεκεν πλέων, τοῦ πλεῖν, ἂν μὴ παρῇ τὸ κερδαίνειν. Ὁ δὲ αὐτὸ δι' ἑαυτὸ τιμῶν τε καὶ περιέπων, ἐπειδὴ τοῦ ἑστῶτος ἐρᾷ, ἑστῶσαν ἔχει καὶ τὴν περὶ αὐτὸ προθυμίαν· ὥστε θεῖόν τι πάσχων, καὶ τὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ δύνασθαι λέγειν· Ἐγὼ δὲ, ὁ αὐ-τός εἰμι, καὶ οὐκ ἠλλοίωμαι. Οὔκουν μεταποιηθήσεται, οὐδὲ μετατεθήσεται. οὐδὲ συμμεταπεσεῖται τοῖς καιροῖς καὶ τοῖς πράγμασιν, ἄλλοτε ἄλλος γινό-μενος, καὶ πολλὰς μεταλαμβάνων χρόας, ὥσπερ τὰς τῶν πετρῶν οἱ πολύποδες, αἷς ἂν ὁμιλήσωσι· μενεῖ δὲ ὁ αὐτὸς ἀεὶ, πάγιος ἐν οὐ πεπηγόσι, καὶ ἐν στρε-φομένοις ἄστροφος· πέτρα τις, οἶμαι, πρὸς ἐμβολὰς ἀνέμων τε καὶ κυμάτων, οὔτε τινασσομένη, καὶ δα-πανῶσα περὶ ἑαυτὴν τὰ προσπίπτοντα. Ταῦτα μὲν εἰς τοσοῦτον· οὐδὲ γάρ μοι σχολὴ ταῖς γλώσσαις μάχεσθαι, καὶ ταῦτα ἴσως πλείω τοῦ δέοντος. Ιʹ. Ἤδη δέ μοι πρὸς ὑμᾶς ὁ λόγος, τὸ ἐμὸν ποίμνιον. Ὑμεῖς γένεσθέ μοι, φησὶν ὁ Παῦλος, δόξα, καὶ χαρὰ, καὶ καυχήσεως στέφανος· ὑμεῖς ἀπολογία τοῖς ἐμὲ ἀνακρίνουσιν· ἵν', ὥσπερ τοῖς τεκτονικοῖς ἢ γραφικοῖς ἀπαιτουμένοις λό-γον, ἐξαρκεῖ δείξασι τὸ τεκτονηθὲν ἢ γραφὲν ἀπηλλάχθαι πραγμάτων (ἔργον γὰρ λόγου, φησὶν, ἰσχυ-ρότερον), οὕτως καὶ αὐτὸς ὑμᾶς ἐπιδείξας, ὑπερ-έξω τὰς λοιδορίας. Ὑπερέξω δὲ πῶς; Πρῶτον μὲν, ἐὰν τὴν εἰς Πατέρα, καὶ Υἱὸν, καὶ ἅγιον Πνεῦμα ὁμολογίαν ἀκλινῆ καὶ βεβαίαν φυλάττητε, μηδὲν προστιθέντες, μηδὲ ἀφαιροῦντες, μηδὲ σμικρύνοντες τῆς μιᾶς Θεότητος (τὸ γὰρ ἐλαττωθὲν, τοῦ παντός ἐστιν ἐλάττωσις)· τοὺς δὲ ἄλλο τι φρονοῦντας, ἢ λέγοντας, ἢ φύσεων μέτροις τὸ ἓν διαλύοντας, ἢ δια-τειχίζοντας, ὡς λύμην τῆς Ἐκκλησίας, καὶ τῆς ἀλη-θείας ἰὸν, ἀποπέμποισθε, μὴ μισοῦντες, ἀλλ' ἐλεοῦν-τες τοῦ πτώματος. Δεύτερον δὲ, εἰ τὴν πολιτείαν ἀκόλουθον τῷ ὀρθῷ λόγῳ παρέχοιτε, ἵν' ἦτε περι-δέξιοι τὴν ἀρετὴν, ἀλλὰ μὴ τῷ ἑτέρῳ λείποντες. ΙΑʹ. Οἱ βασιλεῖς, αἰδεῖσθε τὴν ἁλουργίδα· νομοθε-τήσει γὰρ καὶ νομοθέταις ὁ λόγος. Γινώσκετε ὅσον τὸ πιστευθὲν ὑμῖν, καὶ τί τὸ μέγα περὶ ὑμᾶς μυστή-ριον. Κόσμος ὅλος ὑπὸ χεῖρα τὴν ὑμετέραν, διαδή-ματι μικρῷ καὶ βραχεῖ ῥακίῳ κρατούμενος. Τὰ μὲν ἄνω, μόνου Θεοῦ· τὰ κάτω δὲ, καὶ ὑμῶν. Θεοὶ γέ-νεσθε τοῖς ὑφ' ὑμᾶς, ἵν' εἴπω τι καὶ τολμηρότε-ρον. Καρδία βασιλέως ἐν χειρὶ Θεοῦ, καὶ εἴρηται, καὶ πιστεύεται. Ἐνταῦθα ἔστω τὸ κράτος ὑμῖν, ἀλλὰ μὴ τῷ χρυσῷ καὶ ταῖς φάλαγξιν. Οἱ περὶ τὰ βασί-λεια καὶ τοὺς θρόνους, μὴ σφόδρα ταῖς ἐξουσίαις ἐπαίρεσθε, μηδὲ ἀθάνατα διανοεῖσθε περὶ τῶν οὐκ ἀθανάτων. Πιστοὶ μένετε τοῖς βασιλεῦσι, Θεῷ δὲ πρό-τερον, δι' ὃν καὶ τούτοις οἷς ἐπιστεύθητε, καὶ οἷς παραδέδοσθε. Οἱ τὸ γένος κομπάζοντες, τὸν τρόπον ἐξευγενίσατε· ἢ φθέγξομαί τι τῶν ἀηδῶν μὲν, εὐγε-νῶν δέ. Τότε γὰρ ἀληθὲς εὐγενέστατον ἦν ἄν τι τὸ ὑμέτερον, εἰ μὴ καὶ δέλτοι τοὺς δυσγενεῖς ὑμῖν ἐνέγραφον.
thought_title: Staying the same and holding the confession
orientation: Gregory stops answering accusers and speaks to his own flock and then to emperors and courtiers about guarding the confession of the Trinity with a matching life.
pass_a_gloss: But the seeming, if it is present, we will accept, to say something even human; but if it opposes, we will bid it farewell, and we will take away nothing from being on account of seeming. For so it stands; for the one practicing the good for the sake of something is not firm toward virtue. For at the same time as that thing passes away, he will also stand apart from the good; just as the one sailing for the sake of gain will stand apart from sailing, if gaining is not present. But the one honoring and cherishing it for its own sake, since he loves what stands, also has his eagerness about it standing; so that experiencing something divine, he is also able to say the word of God; But I am the same, and I have not been changed. Therefore he will not be remade, nor moved, nor fall together with the seasons and the affairs, becoming at one time one thing and at another another, and taking many colors, just as the octopuses take the colors of the rocks with which they associate; but he will remain always the same, fixed among things not fixed, and unturned among things turning; a rock, I think, against assaults of winds and waves, neither shaken, and spending upon itself the things falling upon it. These things so far; for I have no leisure to fight tongues, and these words are perhaps more than needed. But now my word is to you, my flock. You become to me, as Paul says, glory and joy and crown of boasting; you are defense to those judging me; so that, just as for builders or painters when asked for an account it suffices after showing what was built or painted to be released from troubles (for a work is stronger than a word, as he says), so also I after showing you will rise above insults. But how will I rise above? First, if you guard the confession into Father and Son and Holy Spirit unbent and firm, adding nothing, taking away nothing, nor making small any of the one Godhead (for what is lessened is a lessening of the whole); and if you send away those who think or say anything else, or who dissolve the One with measures of natures, or who wall it apart, as a harm of the church and a poison of the truth, not hating but pitying the fall. But second, if you present a way of life following right speech, so that you are dexterous on both sides in virtue, but lacking in neither. Kings, revere the purple robe; for speech will legislate even for legislators. Know how great is what was trusted to you, and what is the great mystery concerning you. The whole world is under your hand, held by a small crown and a short rag. The things above are of God alone; but the things below are also yours. Become gods to those under you, to say something even bolder. The heart of a king is in the hand of God, both it has been said and it is believed. Let your strength be here, but not in gold and in phalanxes. You around the palace and the thrones, do not be lifted up greatly by powers, nor think immortal thoughts about things not immortal. Remain faithful to the kings, but first to God, through whom you are also faithful to these kings, by whom you were trusted and by whom you have been handed over. You who boast in birth, make your manner noble; or I will utter something of things unpleasant but noble. For then your nobility would be something truly most noble, if tablets did not also inscribe the ignoble among you.

pass_b_english: As for reputation, I will welcome it, to speak in human terms, when it comes. When it goes against me, I will let it go, and I will sacrifice nothing of being for the sake of seeming. For the matter stands like this. Whoever pursues what is good for the sake of something else has no firm hold on virtue. The moment that other thing passes, he stops pursuing the good. He is like a man who sails for profit and will sail no longer when there is no profit to be found. But whoever honors and cherishes the good for its own sake loves what stands firm, and so his zeal for it stands firm as well. He undergoes something divine, so that he can even speak the words of God, "But I am the same, and I have not changed" (Malachi 3:6).

So he will not be remade or shifted. He will not fall along with times and circumstances, becoming a different man at different moments and taking on many colors, like octopuses taking on the colors of the rocks they cling to. He will remain always the same, fixed among things that are not fixed and unturned among things that turn. He will be, I think, like a rock against the crash of winds and waves, unshaken itself and wearing down upon itself whatever strikes it. Enough of this, for I have no leisure to fight with tongues, and this is already perhaps more than is needed.

Now my words are for you, my flock. Paul says, "Become for me glory and joy and a crown of boasting" (1 Thessalonians 2:19). You are a defense before those who examine me. So just as builders or painters, when called to account, need only point to what they built or painted to be free of trouble, for, as the saying goes, a deed is stronger than a word, so I too shall rise above insults by pointing to you. And how shall I rise above them? First, if you guard unbent and firm your confession in the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, adding nothing, removing nothing, and making nothing small in the one Godhead, for whatever is lessened is a lessening of the whole.

Send away those who think or say anything different, or who dissolve the unity by measuring it with natures or wall it apart, as a defilement of the church and a poison of the truth. Do this without hating them, but pitying their fall. Second, make your way of life follow right teaching, so that you embrace virtue fully and fall short in neither part.

You kings, revere the purple robe, for my sermon will legislate even for lawgivers. Know how great is what has been entrusted to you, and what is the great mystery concerning you. The whole world is under your hand, held by a small diadem and a short rag. What is above belongs to God alone, and what is below belongs also to you. Become gods to those beneath you, to say something even bolder. The heart of a king is in the hand of God (Proverbs 21:1), as has been said and is believed. Let your strength lie there, not in gold and armies. You who stand around the palace and the thrones, do not puff yourselves up too much on your offices, and do not think immortal thoughts about things that are not immortal. Remain faithful to the kings, and first to God, for whose sake you were entrusted to them and given over into their care. You who boast of your birth, ennoble your conduct, or I shall utter something unpleasant but noble. For only then would your birth be truly most noble, if the records did not also list the lowborn alongside you.

problems.source_quote: ἂν μὲν ὑπάρχῃ, δεξόμεθα, ἵν' εἴπω τι καὶ ἀνθρώπινον· ἂν δὲ ἀντιπίπτῃ, χαίρειν ἐάσομεν
problems.why: ὑπάρχῃ means if reputation is present; ἀντιπίπτῃ means if it goes against us, not a test of matching reality.
problems.fix: If reputation comes, I will welcome it, humanly speaking; if it goes against me, I will let it go.
problems.ruling: ὑπάρχῃ means 'is present/exists'; ἀντιπίπτῃ 'opposes'. English 'matches/contradicts what is real' imports a reality test the Greek does not state.

last_rejected.quote: Remain faithful to the kings, and first to God, for whose sake you were entrusted to them and given over into their care.
last_rejected.source_quote: Πιστοὶ μένετε τοῖς βασιλεῦσι, Θεῷ δὲ πρότερον, δι' ὃν καὶ τούτοις οἷς ἐπιστεύθητε, καὶ οἷς παραδέδοσθε.
last_rejected.why: δι’ ὃν continues the command: through God, stay faithful also to those to whom you were entrusted.
last_rejected.fix: Remain faithful to the kings, but to God first, and through him faithful also to these, to whom you were entrusted and handed over.
last_rejected.ruling: δι' ὃν takes the accusative, so it means 'on account of whom' or 'for whose sake'. The English matches, and τούτοις οἷς ἐπιστεύθητε is also rendered correctly.
